verses.text: But Jonah was furious about this. He was angry.

He prayed to the LORD: “LORD, wasn’t this what I said back home? That’s why I rushed to run away to Tarshish. I knew you are gracious and merciful, slow to anger, and full of faithful love—you relent from sending disaster.
“So now, LORD, please take my life. I would rather die than live.”
The LORD said, “Is it right for you to be angry?”
Jonah left the city and sat down east of it. He made a shelter there and sat in its shade, waiting to see what would happen to the city.
The LORD God appointed a plant to grow over Jonah and shade his head, easing his distress. Jonah was very happy about the plant.
But at dawn the next day, God appointed a worm to attack the plant, and it withered.
When the sun came up, God appointed a scorching east wind. The sun beat down on Jonah’s head, and he grew faint. He asked to die, saying, “I would rather die than live.”
God asked Jonah, “Is it right for you to be angry about the plant?” He answered, “Yes! I’m right to be angry—even to the point of death!”
The LORD said, “You cared about the plant, though you didn’t work for it or make it grow. It sprang up in one night and died in one night.
“Shouldn’t I care about Nineveh, that great city with more than 120,000 people who can’t tell their right hand from their left, and also many animals?”
